object: Altar 39 cm. 5 × 37 cm. including the spout.
lines_described: On border, one line of late writing.
first: (1) wosi : so(2)reyi : ẖyre(3)ñ : kroro : mlowitrmy(4)wi : akosyi : terikelowi : syke(5)te : tedḫelowi : ato mẖe : yiẖeke(6)te : at mẖe : aḫ(7)rkete :
final: (1) wosi : so(2)reyi : qore(3)ñ : kroro : mlowitrqo(4)wi : ansyi : terikelowi : syoke(5)li : tedḫelowi : ato mẖe : yiẖeke(6)te : at mẖe : aḫ(7)rkete :
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! The qêreñ-akarêrê Malêwitar : begotten of Anashayi : born of Shayêkeli. (Formulae A B.)

changes.why: Griffith qêreñ: the 3-shaped sign with the stroke on its left is q (/3), the second stroke o
the open 3 with two strokes after Malêwitar is q + o, drawn as in qoreñ (copula qowi; Griffith renders only the name)
Griffith Anashayi: rising stroke + 3 with long tail is n, not k + o
Griffith Shayêkeli: the long fourth stroke of //// is o; the group 45 is l + i, not te

kept.why: no a sign between the divider and k in the copy; the long tail under the divider belongs to k
the copy clearly has s o r e y i; Ashêri is his conventional name for Osiris

unsure.why: 3-shaped sign with long tail; Griffith's akarêrê supports k
open 3 (like m) followed by two strokes; read as q + o by comparison with qoreñ
a dot stands over the right arm of r
the upper dot of the divider is drawn as two short strokes
small S before te; e and l look alike in this hand

notes: Three rows; each row has a right and a left group separated by a wide gap; read right group then left group, rows top to bottom (raised numbers 1-7 run in this order). Each raised number stands just right of the first sign of its line. Formula A (ato mẖe : yiẖekete, initial yi for pšê as Griffith notes for no. 2 on p. 647) then Formula B (at mẖe : aḫrkete). Faint marks above 'reyi' in row 1 look like show-through and were ignored. More than five extra crops were cut for this text.

object: Rectangular stela, with square projection at the top, h. 45 cm., w. 29 cm.
lines_described: coarsely inscribed with nine lines of late writing between rules reaching half way down, the rules continued to the bottom of the stela
first: (1) wo si soreyi qo mli(2)sḫi lo kodib tedḫe li te(3)dḫelo aqkelbenrklo (4)selqenlo lib eesee(5)lo teter be qetelo seo(6)lo ḫerid pesato lit(7)ye[.]m?delo wi si sore(8)yi ato mḫe psoḫeke(9)te at mḫe psḫrkete
final: (1) wo si soreyi qo mli(2)sḫi lo ko?dib tedḫe li te(3)dḫelo amokelbedrplo (4)sleqeñlo lib lesel(5)lo teter be qetelo mlo(6)lo ḫlbiñ pesato lit(7)ye[.]m?delo wi si sore(8)yi ato mḫe psoḫeke(9)te at mḫe psḫrkete
rendering: O Wêsh! O Ashêri! The noble (?) Malishachi : truly born of Kazib : bezarap of the amêke (akhêke?) : shaleqeñ : libalesal : teter in Beqe : malê : kin of a chelabiñ of the pesatê. O Wish! O Ashêri! (Formulae A B.)

changes.why: Griffith Kazib has no vowel between k and d; the short separate stroke is kept but marked unsure
Griffith amêke: /3 is m + o, not q; bezarap: the hooked sign is d and the last long-tailed sign p
Griffith shaleqeñ: the two S-signs are l then e; the ʌ with a long leg is ñ
Griffith libalesal: S-signs are l, e, l; ν// is se
Griffith malê: the 3 is m, the S l
Griffith chelabiñ: the wide ω-like sign is b (ν with long right arm), the T-like sign ñ, the S l

kept.why: a separate short stroke stands between k and d in the copy
only one sign stands between ḫ and b; his chelabiñ implies e + l (he gives Chalabiñ for the Karanòg title)
the copy clearly has s o r e y i (twice)

unsure.why: /3 followed by a short stroke; Griffith gives only 'the noble (?)'
S-sign; e and l look alike; read l for 'of the amêke'
45 + dotted hook; Griffith gives no Latin letters here
a hatched sign with one stroke left, then a single tall stroke before d

unsure.could_be: a stray stroke or part of d
unsure.why: short stroke between k and d not in Griffith's Kazib
Griffith 'in Beqe' is one word; the copy leaves a gap after be

notes: Seven rows, no word dividers; groups separated by gaps written as spaces. Rows read top to bottom, right group then left group; raised numbers 1-9 stand just right of each line's first sign. The second invocation (wi si soreyi, Griffith 'O Wish') stands in row 6 before Formula A (ato mḫe psoḫekete) and Formula B (at mḫe psḫrkete, row 7), as his p. 647 note says for no. 10 (mḫe with ḫ). A small dotted row of four or five specks lies above the left part of row 3, a single dot at the far left of row 2, and a ':'-like mark in the right margin between rows 4 and 5; none was taken as text. More than five extra crops were cut for this text.

Griffith p. 647: mte for ẖte in no. 15

ν-shaped sign where Formula B usually has ḫ
c-shaped sign after a

notes: Four rows read top to bottom, right group then left group. Formulae B A: at mḫ (Griffith p. 648: mḫ in no. 15) : psobrkte, then ato mẖe psmte. While looking for the description of no. 13, low-resolution previews of pp. 613-614 showed the renderings of nos. 14 and 15 before step 1 for these two texts; the first readings were still made sign by sign from the copy.
